explain.say: A wolf pack is usually a family: a mother and father and their offspring from the last few years. Working together, they can bring down elk, moose and bison, far bigger than any one wolf.

explain.say: Wolves track prey by scent, then test a herd by rushing towards it. Healthy animals that stand firm or run strongly are often left alone, while the young, old, sick or injured are picked out.

explain.say: A lone wolf mostly hunts smaller animals like beavers and hares. A pack can take big prey, guard the carcass from scavengers such as ravens and bears, and carry food back to the pups.

faq.q: Why do wolves chase herds before attacking?
faq.a: The first rush is a test. Wolves watch how animals react, and any that stumble, lag or seem weak become the target, because attacking a healthy elk or bison is dangerous.
asks: How do wolves choose which animal to chase?
Why do wolves pick on weak animals?

faq.q: Is there really an alpha wolf?
faq.a: In the wild a pack is usually a family, and the "alphas" are simply the parents, who lead because they are older and more experienced. The idea of fierce alphas fighting for rank came from studies of unrelated wolves kept together in captivity.
asks: Do wolves have a pecking order?

faq.q: How often do wolf hunts succeed?
faq.a: Many hunts of large prey fail. Studies often find that only around one chase in five or fewer ends in a kill when wolves hunt elk or moose.
asks: How many hunts do wolves win?

faq.q: How big is a wolf pack?
faq.a: Most packs have about 5 to 10 wolves, though some have over 20. The size depends on how much prey there is and how many pups survive.
asks: How many wolves are in a pack?
What is the biggest wolf pack?

faq.a: Howling helps pack members find each other over long distances and warns other packs to stay out of their territory. A chorus of howls can carry for kilometres.
asks: What does a wolf howl mean?
Do wolves howl at the moon?

facts: Wild wolf packs are usually families made of a breeding pair and their offspring (Mech, 1999).
A hungry wolf can eat roughly 9 kilograms of meat in one meal.
